text:
Chicago lost 9-2 in Carolina on Saturday and held a players' meeting afterward. Wyatt Kaiser told The Athletic's Mark Lazerus the team needs to "ball up" and figure out how "to get out of this." It's six without a win (0-5-1), outscored 32-13, and our numbers say the slide is earned: the Blackhawks got 36 percent of the expected goals in that stretch, and our simulations put their playoff chances at zero.

Pressure is landing on Jeff Blashill. Connor Bedard has publicly backed his coach, which tells you the question is being asked. Patrick Kane's upper-body injury took away a top-line winger, and Arvid Soderblom has saved 4.7 fewer goals than expected over his last four starts. Tyler Bertuzzi has one point in ten games against chances worth 5.4.

The bright spot is Roman Kantserov, the rookie the Sun-Times and the New York Times have both singled out. The Kaiser and Artyom Levshunov pairing has been outscored 15-4, which is the kind of number that makes a young defenseman's development harder, not easier. If you follow Chicago right now, you're watching for the coach's job, Bedard's mood and Kantserov's goals, roughly in that order.
headline: The Blackhawks are bottoming out, and the room knows it
